Comet builder — a SF_KINDS.COMET body is a dark
Source src/experiments/star-field/engine/bodies/comet.ts
UX surface Boot surfaces: what the user sees first on each bundle.

Members

SF_USER_GAS_TILT

userData key stashing a gas plane's fixed z-tilt — updateFx reads it to un-rotate the camera vector back into the frame where the streak axis is local +x before solving the cylindrical-billboard roll.

TAIL_W

Tail gradient canvas — long narrow streak, alpha fades along +x.

gasFor

Paints the streaming-gas layer texture: a horizontally TILEABLE filament field (wrapS = RepeatWrapping) so updateFx can roll map.offset.x and the gas visibly streams anti-sunward like plasma riding the solar wind. The tail silhouette is NOT painted here — it lives in the plane's vertex colors (scroll-invariant), so this texture must stay seamless: every wisp follows y(x) = mid + sin(2π·cycles·x/W + φ)·amp with an INTEGER cycle count, so the path's phase at the left edge equals the right edge; knot clumps are each drawn at x ± W to wrap blobs that straddle the seam.

  • @param THREE The three.js module.
  • @param seed Deterministic RNG stream (seeded per tail so the ion and
  • @returns A tileable CanvasTexture, or undefined without a 2d context.

for

Filaments — thin sinuous rays running the tail's length. Integer cycles keeps the sine periodic across the canvas width (the wrap seam is invisible); each streak's alpha jitters so the sheet reads as braided streamers, not one uniform smear.

for

Knots — denser gas clumps the outgassing vents throw, biased toward the root (real comae are thickest at the nucleus). Painted at both x and x ± W so a blob crossing the wrap seam shows its continuation on the far edge.

tailFor

Paints the shared tail sprite texture: a horizontal gradient that is brightest at the left edge (the end rooted at the nucleus) and fades smoothly to nothing on the right (the tip dissolving into space), with a vertical cosine falloff so the streak is a soft spindle, not a hard-edged ribbon. White-only — the SpriteMaterial color supplies the ion/dust tint so one texture serves both tails.

  • @param THREE The three.js module.
  • @returns A CanvasTexture, or undefined without a 2d context.

makeComet

Builds the comet composite: an irregular, nearly-black nucleus (the real Halley albedo is ~0.04 — one of the darkest known bodies), a soft additive coma sprite hugging it, and the ion + dust tail sprites. The nucleus mesh becomes the node's mesh/spinner so it tumbles normally; coma rides inside it (a symmetric billboard is indifferent to spin); the tails mount on center where local +x is permanently anti-sunward.

  • @param THREE The three.js module.
  • @param def Catalog entry — radius sizes the nucleus; ecc/orbit
  • @param texMap Loaded texture map (a comet with a real nucleus map
  • @param glowTex Shared radial-glow texture for the coma sprite.
  • @returns { mesh, coma, ion, dust, ionGas, dustGas } — the pickable

tailSprite

One tail sprite — camera-facing, so the streak reads from every angle. Its center sits at len/2 along +x so the texture's bright root edge lands on the nucleus and the fade runs anti-sunward. tilt swings the sprite's origin off the ecliptic plane so the dust fan visibly lags the ion streak.

gasPlane

Gas layer — a highly tessellated PLANE that updateFx rolls around the tail axis to face the camera (a cylindrical billboard): unlike a camera-facing sprite it has true spatial extent (it is a real streak of gas sitting in the scene, not a postcard), and unlike a cone it can never expose a polygonal silhouette. The silhouette is carried by PER-VERTEX COLORS, not the texture: b = ramp(t)·(1−w²)^p fades axial position t (0 root → 1 tip) AND transverse offset w (−1…1), so every quad edge lands at black — which additive blending renders as fully transparent. Because the envelope is geometry-side, the seamless filament map can scroll offset.x forever without dragging the fade with it — gas genuinely streams anti-sunward through a static soft envelope.
